summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Australian documents on the Business Innovation and Investment Program (BIIP), the Significant Investor visa (SIV), the Investor stream and the Premium Investor visa: five 2014 Senate Estimates answers, the 2019 consultation paper and 2020 review report, the CIF FAQ, the BP0068 Migration Program workbook, six Home Affairs FOI releases and five visa web pages. Added every monthly, citizenship, government-sponsor, applicant-type and stream cell from the FOI tables and Senate answers ("<5" as 1-4), the investor-stream splits of the BP0068 pivot cache (citizenship, gender, state, age, lodging location, subclass), processing-time percentiles, withdrawal rates, on-hand counts, EOIs and invitations, and the stream rules (CIF proportions, assets, fees, residence days, visa lengths). Tables add up to their printed totals except the FA 20/12/01057 lodged grand total (495 printed, the yearly totals sum to 993). BP0068 is partial: non-investor BIIP streams are taken only as totals by applicant type.

observations.location: p. 2, 'Program overview', last paragraph
observations.quote: In 2019-20, 6,862 visa places have been allocated to the BIIP, representing 6.3% of the skill stream of the migration program.
observations.notes: BIIP planning level as a share of the 2019-20 Skill stream planning level (108,682), as printed by the department.

observations.location: p. 1, sixth bullet
observations.quote: Since 2014-15 places were set at 7,260, places were reduced in 2019-20 to 6,862, and increased to 13,500 in 2020-21.
observations.notes: Planning level for BIIP places, the same in each programme year from 2014-15 until the 2019-20 reduction ("Since 2014-15 places were set at 7,260"); one row for the span as printed, not split by year.

observations.location: p. 1, sixth bullet
observations.quote: Since 2014-15 places were set at 7,260, places were reduced in 2019-20 to 6,862, and increased to 13,500 in 2020-21.
observations.notes: Planning level for BIIP places.

observations.location: p. 1, seventh bullet
observations.quote: The BIIP made up 4.6% of the Skilled stream grants in 2019-20.
observations.notes: BIIP grants (primary and secondary, Migration Program places) as a share of all Skill stream grants in 2019-20, as printed. The base is Skill stream grants, not all first-time residence permits.

observations.location: p. 2, last bullet
observations.quote: 41 written submissions were received and nine roundtable discussions were held
observations.notes: Written submissions to the BIIP review consultation (opened 19 Dec 2019, closed 14 Feb 2020).

observations.location: p. 2, last bullet
observations.quote: 41 written submissions were received and nine roundtable discussions were held
observations.notes: Roundtable discussions held for the BIIP review (with state and territory governments, Commonwealth agencies, fund managers and migration agents). Printed in words ("nine").

observations.location: PDF p. 8, Q&A 'Will the outcomes of the 2017 business, investment and talent visas review be published?'
observations.quote: since 2012, Significant Investor visa holders have invested more than $11.4 billion in Australia’s economy
observations.notes: Internal Home Affairs briefing (talking points cleared 11 Dec 2019), released under FOI FA 20/08/00701. "More than"; a lower bound. Period runs from 2012 to an unstated end (the briefing is dated December 2019; p. 9 gives the same figure to end of November 2019). Printed with a bare "$" (Australian dollars by context).

observations.location: PDF p. 9, 'Since the BIIP was introduced in July 2012 to end of November 2019', first bullet
observations.quote: 1,193 primary provisional Investor visas have been granted, bringing a total investment of about 1.79 billion in Australian state and territory government bonds.
observations.notes: Internal Home Affairs briefing (talking points cleared 11 Dec 2019), released under FOI FA 20/08/00701. Primary provisional Investor stream visas. The 2019 consultation paper gives the same 1,193 "as of 31 October 2019".

observations.location: PDF p. 9, same bullet
observations.quote: bringing a total investment of about 1.79 billion in Australian state and territory government bonds
observations.notes: Internal Home Affairs briefing (talking points cleared 11 Dec 2019), released under FOI FA 20/08/00701. "About"; no currency written. Equals 1,193 grants times the AUD1.5 million minimum, so it is the required investment, not measured investment.

events.title: Immigration minister foreshadows a "reboot" of the Significant Investor visa
events.description: In an address to the Migration Institute of Australia National Conference in Canberra, Immigration and Border Protection Minister Scott Morrison foreshadowed a "reboot" of the SIV (as recalled in the department's answer SE14/445).
events.quote: In his address of 21 October 2013 to the Migration Institute of Australia National Conference, Canberra, the former Minister for Immigration and Border Protection, the Hon. Scott Morrison MP, foreshadowed a “reboot” of the SIV.

events.title: Parliamentary committee asked to inquire into the BIIP, excluding the Significant Investor stream
events.description: The government asked the Joint Standing Committee on Migration to inquire into and report on the Business Innovation and Investment Programme, excluding the SIV stream, which was under a departmental review.
events.quote: On 18 March 2014 the government made a request to the Joint Standing Committee on Migration (JSCM) that they inquire into and report on the Business Innovation and Investment Programme (BIIP), excluding the SIV stream.

events.title: BIIP review consultation closes (41 written submissions)
events.description: The public consultation for the Business Innovation and Investment program review closed; 41 written submissions were received and nine roundtables held. Most submissions on the Premium Investor visa suggested closing it.
events.quote: The consultation process closed on 14 February 2020.

events.title: New Complying Investment Framework ratios (20/30/50) for Significant Investor and Investor streams; annual fund audits
events.description: From 1 July 2021 the Complying Investment Framework (IMMI 15/100 as amended by LIN 21/041) requires 20% in venture capital and growth private equity funds, 30% in emerging-company funds and 50% in balancing investments, and applies to the Investor stream as well as the Significant Investor stream. Funds offering emerging-companies or balancing components must provide annual independent audit reports of CIF compliance.
events.quote: From 1 July 2021 the CIF ratios will apply to both the Investor and the Significant Investor streams as follows:

new_indicators.name: Programme planning level as a share of a wider planning category
new_indicators.definition: Planned visa places for a programme as a percentage of a wider planning category (e.g. the Skill stream of Australia's Migration Program) in a programme year, as printed by the source. A target, so status is budget. Use breakdown category= for the wider category.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for the BIIP share of the 2019-20 Skill stream (6.3%) in the 2019 Home Affairs consultation paper.

new_indicators.name: Responses to a public consultation on a programme
new_indicators.definition: Number of written submissions, roundtables or other responses received in a government's public consultation or review of an investment-migration programme, as printed by the source. Use breakdown category= for the kind of response; unit says what is counted.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for the December 2020 Home Affairs BIIP review report (41 written submissions, nine roundtables).

new_indicators.name: Expressions of interest submitted
new_indicators.definition: Expressions of interest (EOIs) for an investor visa held or submitted in an invitation system (e.g. Australia's SkillSelect) at a date or in a period, before any invitation to apply. Notes say whether a stock at a date or a flow.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for SIV EOIs by nominating government (FOI FA 20/08/00701, EOIs as at 31 March 2019).

new_indicators.name: Invitations to apply issued
new_indicators.definition: Invitations to apply for an investor visa issued to people who lodged an expression of interest (and, where relevant, were nominated), in a period.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for Australian SIV invitations (FOI FA 20/08/00701).

new_indicators.name: Application withdrawal rate
new_indicators.definition: Applications withdrawn as a percentage of applications (or of finalised applications), in a period, as printed by the source; notes give the source's base. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for the Australian SIV (33.7% in 2018-19; and the withdrawal rates in FOI FA 21/10/01119).

new_indicators.name: Share of applicant documents verified
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of a type of supporting document (business ownership, qualifications, patents) that a processing office verifies with the issuing authority, as stated by the source at a date.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus1 for a Nov 2019 Home Affairs email (FOI FA 20/08/00701).

ledger.contains: One-page Senate Estimates answer (AE14/212): 129 primary Significant Investor visa grants between 1 Sep 2013 and 28 Feb 2014; notes that statistics are available only by calendar month. The one number is already in the data (not duplicated).

One-page Senate Estimates answer (AE14/213): new SIV investment options under Instrument IMMI 13/092 from 23 Nov 2013 (listed bonds/equity/hybrids, annuities, derivatives for portfolio management, mortgage-secured loans); SIV threshold unchanged at $5 million; 69 primary SIV grants 1 Dec 2013-28 Feb 2014 with $345 million in complying investments. Both numbers and the IMMI 13/092 event are already in the data; the $5 million threshold is already a rule row from the 2019 discussion paper (not duplicated).

One-page Senate Estimates answer (BE14/475) on reports commissioned: the Internal Review of the SIV programme, commissioned 7 Mar 2014, given to government 28 May 2014, not released; terms of reference (policy settings, benefits, processing, a national stream free of state nomination, promotion); cost $73 494 and staff (EL 1.45, APS 1.2). Cost and staff added; the review dates are already in event e-df747d0092.

One-page Senate Estimates answer (SE14/445): Morrison foreshadowed an SIV "reboot" on 21 Oct 2013; departmental SIV review announced 7 Mar 2014; JSCM asked on 18 Mar 2014 to inquire into the BIIP excluding the SIV; no plans to change the $5 million SIV threshold; the new Premium Investor visa from July 2015 will have a $15 million threshold. Added events for 21 Oct 2013 and 18 Mar 2014 (the 7 Mar 2014 review event already exists from this source). The $5m and $15m thresholds are already rule rows (from the 2019 discussion paper and the 2019 PIV page); no statistics.

One-page Senate Estimates answer (SE14/446): SIV primary grants and complying investment in 2013-14 (282; $1.41 billion) and 1 Mar-30 Nov 2014 (372; $1.86 billion); monthly table Mar-Nov 2014 of primary applications, grants, rejections and withdrawals with totals; reasons for refusal not reportable. Totals and the two investment figures were already in the data; added the 36 monthly cells, which add up to the printed totals.

Home Affairs consultation paper (Dec 2019) "Getting a better deal for Australia": 2017 review findings (2,264 primary SIV grants to 31 Oct 2019, over $11.32 billion SIV investment); BIIP structure (three visas, nine streams); 2019-20 planning levels (BIIP 6,862 places, 6.3% of the skill stream; the rest of the planning table is other Migration Program categories, out of scope); Investor ($1.5m, July 2012) and SIV ($5m, Nov 2012) thresholds; SIV Complying Investment Framework from July 2015 (10% VCPE, 30% emerging companies, balance with a 10% residential real estate cap); 1,193 primary Investor visas to 31 Oct 2019 and $1.79 billion in state bonds; over $250 billion of state bonds on issue (general bond market figure, out of scope; the "less than 0.7%" share is about the bond market); points test pass mark 65 and full points table; consultation questions; submissions due 14 Feb 2020. Earlier rows (grants, investment, planning level, thresholds, launch events) not duplicated; added the 6.3% share (new indicator proposed), the CIF component minimums and real estate cap, the pass mark and all 28 points-table cells as rules.

Home Affairs slide-style report (Dec 2020) on the BIIP review: BIIP description; planning levels (7,260 from 2014-15, 6,862 in 2019-20, 13,500 in 2020-21); BIIP 4.6% of Skill stream grants in 2019-20; 2012 replacement of Business Skills; top ten nationalities for BIIP grants (a ranking without numbers: China, Vietnam, Malaysia, Iran, Hong Kong, South Africa, India, Bangladesh, UK, Taiwan; not turned into numbers); consultation 19 Dec 2019-14 Feb 2020 with 41 submissions and nine roundtables; summary of stakeholder views given only in words ("one fifth", "more than half", "two thirds"; suggested SIV $6-10m and IV $2-3m thresholds are opinions, not rules); outcomes from 1 July 2021 (nine to four streams, PIV/SBH/VCE closed, five-year provisional visa, PR after three years, SIV two 2-year extensions, BI one 2-year extension, BI assets $1.25m and turnover $750,000, Entrepreneur $200,000 funding threshold scrapped). Added planning levels, the 4.6% share, consultation counts (new indicator proposed), the dated rules and the consultation-close event; 13,500 and the 2019 and 2021 events were already in the data.

Home Affairs BP0068 workbook: Migration Program (and Child) outcomes 2015-16 to 2024-25 as a pivot table over a 622,425-record cache with fields programme year, visa program/category/type/sub-type/subclass, citizenship country, gender, applicant type, age group, client location, occupation (five levels) and intended residence. The visible sheet shows only Migration Program totals by category (Family, Skilled, Special Eligibility, Child), which are out of scope. In scope: the Business Innovation and Investment visa type and its streams, and the legacy investor subclasses 165 and 893. Extracted (by summing the pivot cache with the filters named in each location, as the earlier rows do): for the Significant Investor, Significant Investor Extension, Investor and Premium Investor streams, subclasses 165 and 893, and the BIIP visa type as a whole, every year with records: total, primary, secondary, by citizenship country (all, primary, secondary), by gender, by intended state, by age group, by client location and by visa subclass; for the other BIIP sub-types (Business Innovation, Business Innovation Extension, Entrepreneur, Significant Business History, Venture Capital Entrepreneur, Business Skills, State/Territory Sponsored Business Skills): total, primary and secondary per year. Stream (sub-type) detail exists only from 2017-18; 2015-16 and 2016-17 BIIP grants sit under Business Skills sub-types. Every split adds up to its total (checked). Some cells are negative as stored (BIIP 2022-23: Yemen -5, Myanmar -1, Syria -1; 2024-25: South Korea -1; Business Skills sub-type 2017-18 -1), recorded as stored with a note. Zero cells are not recorded. Four 188 records under Global Talent (Independent) in 2021-22 are outside the BIIP visa type and not taken. Occupation is "Not Specified" for all investor-stream primaries (not extracted).
ledger.to_do: Not extracted from the pivot cache: (1) for the non-investor BIIP sub-types (Business Innovation, Business Innovation Extension, Entrepreneur, Significant Business History, Venture Capital Entrepreneur, Business Skills, State/Territory Sponsored Business Skills) the splits by citizenship country, gender, intended state, age group, client location and subclass; (2) for all streams, cross-splits other than applicant type x citizenship (e.g. citizenship x gender, citizenship x state, age x applicant type); (3) occupation fields (all Not Specified for investor-stream primaries; populated for some other BIIP primaries).
